consensus_summary: Biblical 'shadow' is polyvalent with no single settled primary meaning; the two most prominent senses are divine protection/refuge (under wings or shade of the Almighty) and typological foreshadowing (OT institutions as shadow of Christ/substance), with common alternatives for life's transience and the shadow of death/gloom.
book_summary: Covering of a greater presence: refuge under the Almighty's wings, a kingdom's protection over its people, and the outline a coming body casts ahead of itself; good to dwell in (not gloom), with KJV rendering the word as 'defence'.
consensus_core_identification: Polyvalent image whose dominant uses are divine protection/refuge or typological foreshadowing of Christ, treated as separate context-dependent senses.
book_core_identification: Covering of a greater presence that unifies refuge/protection and the outline cast by a coming body, positive and good to dwell in rather than gloom.
boundary_disagreement: Book unifies the two dominant consensus senses (protection and typology) as aspects of one covering-of-greater-presence idea, adds kingdom-defence example, and excludes gloom/transience as misreadings, whereas consensus keeps the senses separate and lists gloom/death as common.
material_contradiction: None on the included referents; book only rejects the gloom reading that consensus lists as a common alternative.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap on the two dominant senses (protection and typology) attested across all consensus responses. The book preserves those referents but materially refines their relation and boundaries by treating them as a single positive covering, adding the Num 14:9 defence case, and excluding gloom; this is boundary adjustment rather than replacement of the central category.
strongest_objection: Unifying protective and typological uses under one 'covering' may blur distinct scriptural contexts, and dismissing 'shadow of death' ignores a frequent and well-attested biblical phrase.
